Fa' solo che io possieda davvero le cose
che sempre ho disprezzato e trascurato.

en_overlay.rsa-01:
Main establishing/regulatory legislation: Regional Law (RL) of 31 July 2007, No. 32, "Regional rules on authorisation, institutional accreditation and contractual agreements for public and private healthcare and social-healthcare facilities"; recent implementing measures: Regional Council Resolution (DGR) 374 of 28 June 2023, DGR 192 of 8 March 2024, DGR 553 of 28 August 2025.

Breakdown by level/intensity of care: traceable to the national R1/R2/R2D/R3 grid of the Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) of 12 January 2017; the regional act setting out the detailed requirements could not be located in full text — `n.a.`

Essential authorisation requirements: `n.a.` (RL 32/2007 defines the procedure and the types of facility subject to authorisation, deferring to Regional Executive measures for quantitative standards).

Notes: Abruzzo operates under a healthcare deficit recovery plan (piano di rientro), with commissioner and Regional Executive measures progressively updating the requirements; the Guidelines for Social and Health Care Integration of the Regional Social Plan (PSR) 2022-2024 provide the reference planning framework. ---
en_overlay.rsa-02:
Main establishing/regulatory legislation: Regional Council Resolution (DGR) 1218 of 14 November 2017, minimum structural, technological and organisational requirements for health and social care facilities, implementing the Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) of 12 January 2017, preceded by DGR 504 of 1 June 2017 granting final approval (legislative summary, unofficial editorial source); regional institutional page on the provisions for the authorisation of health and social care facilities.

Breakdown by level/intensity: Intensive nursing home – RSA, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali – (R1), RSA for non-self-sufficient persons, RSA for persons with disabilities, as well as facilities for mental disorders, addictions and hospices; the treatment levels considered are R1, R2, R2D Dementia, R2D Alzheimer's Unit, R3, SR, SR2D (criteria for determining need, annex to Regional Council Resolution DGR 574, text reproduced from an unofficial editorial source).

Essential authorisation requirements: for R1, intensive treatment involving a high level of healthcare input with support for vital functions; for R2, continuity of care and 24-hour nursing presence (annex to Regional Council Resolution DGR 574); maximum capacity and minutes of care per resident: `n.a.`

Notes: the operational definition of nursing home (RSA, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali) adopted by the Azienda Sanitaria di Potenza – the Potenza Local Health Authority – confirms this framework. The full official texts of Regional Council Resolutions (DGR) 1218/2017 and 504/2017 were not directly accessible on the regional portal. ---
en_overlay.rsa-03:
Main founding/regulatory legislation: Regional Regulation No. 6 of 21 January 2019, "Non-hospital residential care with high healthcare intensity – RSA R1" (text reproduced from an unofficial publishing source); authorisation requirements for community-based non-hospital facilities are set out in Annex 4 to the regional regulations and in the Accreditation Manual for Community-Based Non-Hospital Facilities (Annex 12).

Structure by level/intensity of care: level R1 is specifically governed by Regional Regulation 6/2019, which covers care with high healthcare intensity; levels R2/R2D/R3 for older persons are mapped onto the Essential Levels of Care (LEA) framework and governed by the annexes on requirements for community-based non-hospital facilities. Detailed breakdown by level: `n.a.`

Essential authorisation requirements: set out in Annex 4 – authorisation requirements for community-based non-hospital facilities; specific values for capacity and care minutes: `n.a.`

Notes: Region subject to a healthcare deficit recovery plan (piano di rientro); regulatory output proceeds mainly through Commissioner's Decrees and regulations, with frequent rewrites of the technical annexes. ---
en_overlay.rsa-04:
Main establishing/regulatory legislation: Regional Law (RL) no. 8 of 22 April 2003 (establishing nursing homes – RSAs, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali – for non-self-sufficient older persons); Decree no. 74 of 9 October 2019, RSA requirements (text reproduced from an unofficial trade association source); Campania Regional Council Resolution (DGRC) no. 269 of 16 May 2023 on additional accreditation requirements.

Breakdown by level/intensity: care units R1, R2, R2D, R3, RD3, consistent with Article 30 of the Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) of 12 January 2017 (Decree 74/2019).

Essential authorisation requirements: RSAs are organised into units of no more than 20 residents (Regional Law 8/2003); staffing standards for each level are set out in Decree 74/2019.

Notes: the Region is already subject to a healthcare deficit recovery plan (piano di rientro); the healthcare authorisation framework is separate from the social-care framework under Regional Regulation (RR) 4/2014. ---
en_overlay.rsa-05:
Main establishing/regulatory legislation: the name "RSA" (nursing homes, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali) has been superseded: the type currently in force is the Casa residenza per anziani non autosufficienti (CRA – residential home for non-self-sufficient older persons), which incorporates the former Casa protetta, or sheltered home, and RSAs. Operating authorisation: point 1.4 of Regional Council Resolution (DGR) 564/2000; accreditation: DGR 514/2009, Annex D, point D.2.3, together with DGR 2110/2009, 664/2017 and 1625/2022; overall regulatory framework on health and social care accreditation.

Breakdown by level/intensity of care: the CRA admits non-self-sufficient older persons with moderate and high levels of dependency, with the possibility of dedicated units for behavioural disorders, high healthcare needs and severe disabilities (consolidated text of Regional Council Resolution DGR 564/2000).

Essential authorisation requirements: as a rule, a maximum of 75 residential places, organised in units of approximately 20–30 people; facilities with a larger capacity may in no case exceed 120 places and must likewise be organised in units of 20–30 people (consolidated text of Regional Council Resolution DGR 564/2000).

Notes: the Region with the clearest terminological rationalisation in Italy; the abandonment of the acronym RSA – nursing homes, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali – in favour of CRA is explicit in regional acts. ---
en_overlay.rsa-06:
Main founding/regulatory legislation: Regional Council Resolution (DGR) 650 of 11 April 2013 on nursing homes (RSA, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali) and hospices; institutional accreditation is governed by Decree of the President of the Region (D.P.Reg.) No. 0107/Pres. of 18 August 2022, implementing Article 64 of Regional Law (RL) 22/2019, with the list of accredited facilities most recently updated by Decree No. 56606 of 28 October 2025.

Organisation by level/intensity: first-, second- and third-level residential facilities under Decree of the President of the Region (D.P.Reg.) 0107/Pres. of 2022 (institutional accreditation page).

Essential authorisation requirements: requirements laid down by Decree of the President of the Region (D.P.Reg.) 144/2015 for operating authorisation and by D.P.Reg. 0107/Pres./2022 for accreditation; specific minimum care-time standards in minutes: `n.a.`

Notes: in FVG, the nursing home (RSA, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali) has historically been a transitional, healthcare-oriented facility (post-acute care/extensive rehabilitation), distinct from the "case di riposo" – rest homes – run by the public personal care service agencies (ASP) and from the residential services for older persons governed by D.P.Reg. 144/2015. ---
en_overlay.rsa-07:
Main establishing/regulatory legislation: Regional Law (RL) no. 4 of 3 March 2003 – operating authorisation for healthcare activities; Commissioner's Decree (DCA) U0008 of 10 February 2011, Annex C – specific requirements for residential facilities; Regional Council Resolution (DGR) 979 of 11 December 2020, Annex A; procedures managed through the regional platform (institutional page on authorisation and accreditation).

Structure by level/intensity of care: Nursing homes – RSA, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali – with units at level R1 (high healthcare intensity), R2/R2D and R3; Residenze Protette (R.P.) – sheltered residences – placed within the senescence care area at level R3 (DCA U0008/2011 Annex C).

Essential authorisation requirements: Nursing homes (RSA): minimum 20 and maximum 80 beds, exceptionally up to 120; organised into units of 10 to 20 beds; R1 units of 4 to 10 beds (DCA U0008/2011 Annex C).

Notes: the common general requirements are set out in DPCA 8/2011 – Decree of the President acting as Commissioner ad acta; the management of authorisation procedures moved to the new regional information system (SANSIAA) as of January 2026. ---
en_overlay.rsa-08:
Main establishing/regulatory legislation: Regional Council Resolution (DGR) 944 of 16 November 2018, updated by DGR 387/2023 and incorporated into the Manual of Requirements for Operating Authorisation.

Structure by level/intensity: First-tier RSA nursing homes – Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali – for rehabilitation/post-acute care and maintenance RSAs, alongside which there is the sheltered residence (Residenza Protetta), with a lower level of healthcare intensity (ASL 2 Liguria Local Health Authority, residential care in RSAs and RPs).

Essential authorisation requirements: defined for each care module in the A.Li.Sa. manual; specific care-minute values: `n.a.`

Notes: Liguria has adopted a "modular" approach that allows modules of differing intensity to coexist within the same facility. ---
en_overlay.rsa-09:
Main establishing/regulatory legislation: Regional Council Resolution (DGR) VII/7435 of 14 December 2001, requirements for the operating authorisation and accreditation of nursing homes (RSA, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali), pursuant to Art. 12 of Regional Law 31/1997; DGR VII/12618 of 7 April 2003, staffing standards and reorganisation of the RSA system (text reproduced from an unofficial source).

Structure by level/intensity of care: abolition of the previous distinction between Protected Care Units (NAP – Nuclei di Assistenza Protetta) and Supervised Care Units (NAT – Nuclei di Assistenza Tutelare) in favour of a single facility standard, with the option of dedicated Alzheimer's units (Regional Council Resolution 12618/2003).

Essential authorisation requirements: overall care standard of 901 minutes per resident per week for accreditation, covering care and healthcare staff (Regional Council Resolution 12618/2003).

Notes: the 901-minutes-per-week standard remains the defining parameter of the Lombardy model; the framework was subsequently supplemented by Regional Law (RL) 23/2015 reforming the social and healthcare system. ---
en_overlay.rsa-10:
Main establishing/regulatory legislation: Regional Law (RL) 21/2016; Regional Council Resolution (DGR) 938/2020 and requirements manual, Part C "Requirements for Facilities for Older Persons – Frailty"; Operating manual approved by Executive Decree (DD) 57/AUA of 2022.

Breakdown by level/intensity: R1 Intermediate care, R2 nursing home – RSA – for non-self-sufficient persons, R2D RSA for dementia, R3 Residenza Protetta – protected residence – for older persons, R3D Residenza Protetta for dementia (Regional Council Resolution 938/2020, Part C).

Essential authorisation requirements: for level R1 (intermediate care): a maximum of 20 beds per unit and a maximum of 2 units per facility, healthcare assistant – OSS – ≥ 106 minutes/day per resident, nurse ≥ 54 minutes/day, physician ≥ 15 minutes/day, physiotherapist 15 minutes/day for 6 days, 24-hour nursing and OSS presence, length of stay of 30 days, extendable by a further 30 (Regional Council Resolution 938/2020, Part C).

Notes: the manual of Regional Council Resolution (DGR) 938/2020 is one of the most detailed in Italy in terms of explicit care minutes per level. ---
en_overlay.rsa-11:
Main founding/regulatory legislation: Regional Regulation 1/2015, Arts. 50–53 — Protected Social and Health Care Residence for Older Persons (RPS, code D3/M3L) and RSA nursing homes (code D6/M3L); Regional Council Resolution (DGR) 738 of 13 July 2009, "Manual of Requirements for Social and Health Care Facilities".

Breakdown by level/intensity: classification into levels R2, R2D, R3 with differentiated tariffs (regional document on classification and tariffs).

Essential authorisation requirements: `n.a.` (the required care minutes per level could not be found in an accessible official source).

Notes: region subject to a healthcare deficit recovery plan; the Manual of Health Authorisations annexed to Commissioner's Decree DCA 36 (unofficial publisher source) supplements the structural requirements (for pre-existing facilities, rooms with up to 4 beds are permitted). ---
en_overlay.rsa-12:
Main establishing/regulatory legislation: Regional Council Resolution (DGR) of 30 July 2012, no. 45-4248, "The new integrated model of residential and semi-residential social and healthcare provision for non-self-sufficient older persons", as amended by DGR 85-6287/2013 (consolidated text published by an unofficial source); summary overview on the institutional page of the Piedmont Region.

Breakdown by level/intensity: care bands: NAT – Nucleo Alzheimer Temporaneo, temporary Alzheimer's unit, high, enhanced level, high, medium-high, medium, medium-low, low, which replace the previous classification under Regional Council Resolution (DGR) 17-15226/2005; in addition, there are the Special Veterans' Units (NSV, Nuclei Speciali Veterani) and the High Complexity Units (NAC, Nuclei Alta Complessità) provided for by DGR 62-13647/2010 (DGR 45-4248/2012).

Essential authorisation requirements: Nursing homes (RSA, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali) with 20 to 120 beds, organised into units of 10 or 20 beds, with the option of 2 or 4 additional beds for emergency admissions; NATs may have a maximum of 2 units of 10 or 20 beds (DGR 45-4248/2012).

Notes: the Piedmont model links the care band to the needs profile identified by the Geriatric Assessment Unit (UVG), with fees differentiated by band. ---
en_overlay.rsa-13:
Main establishing/regulatory legislation: Regional Regulation No. 4 of 21 January 2019, "Residential and semi-residential care for non-self-sufficient persons – extensive and maintenance RSA – Day Centre"; Regional Law No. 53 of 12 December 2017, "Reorganisation of Apulian social and healthcare facilities for residential care for non-self-sufficient persons"; historical framework in RR 8/2002, DGR 210/2002, RL 8/2004, RR 3/2006, RL 26/2006, RL 4/2010, RL 5/2011, RL 15/2021.

Notes: Regional Council Resolution (DGR) 2152/2019 and DGR 1572/2023 continued the process of aligning the facilities governed by RR 4/2007 with the Essential Levels of Care (LEA) set out in the Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) of 12 January 2017. ---
en_overlay.rsa-14:

Salute) No. 79 of 26 January 2026 on updating the regional planning of the residential care network for frail persons (details taken from an editorial repertory, unofficial source: verify the text in the Official Gazette of the Sicilian Region). ---
en_overlay.rsa-16:
Main establishing/regulatory legislation: Decree of the President of the Regional Executive (D.P.G.R.) No. 2/R of 9 January 2018, Art. 21, para. 1, let. a – "Residential facility for non-self-sufficient older persons (Residenza Sanitaria Assistenziale)"; institutional informational overview of nursing homes (RSAs).

en_overlay.rsa-17:

Breakdown by level/intensity of care: the annual Directives define the levels of care and the related staffing parameters (Table A of the Directives) (2025 RSA Directives).

Essential authorisation requirements: staffing parameters set annually in Table A of the RSA Directives (DGP 2253/2024); specific numerical values for 2026: `n.a.`

en_overlay.rsa-18:

Structure by level/intensity of care: intensive care / high-intensity care (SCU) units, extended care units and units for people with dementia (DGP 888/2024).

Notes: the authorisation and accreditation process is described in the technical documentation of the Aziende ULSS (Local Health Authorities). --- ## Final methodological note 1. Number of administrations covered: 21 profiles have been drawn up, corresponding to the 19 ordinary- and special-statute Regions with their own regulations plus the 2 Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano, in the mandatory order set out in the brief. The Trentino-Alto Adige Region has no regulations of its own in this area, as competence is entirely devolved to the two Autonomous Provinces (which therefore bring the overall count to 22 administrations considered). 2. en_overlay.rsa-nazionale-01:
The founding act: Article 20 of Law No. 67 of 11 March 1988

Nursing homes (RSA, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali) came into being as an autonomous legal category with Article 20 of Law No. 67 of 11 March 1988 (1988 Finance Law), which authorises the extraordinary multi-year programme of investment in healthcare buildings and technologies and explicitly earmarks a share of the resources for the «construction of residences for older persons and non-self-sufficient individuals who cannot be cared for at home». It is this provision that introduces the RSA into the national legislative vocabulary as a non-hospital facility intended for non-self-sufficient individuals, distinct both from hospitals and from purely social-care facilities such as rest homes and group homes, which fall under regional and municipal responsibility.
The technical and programming framework of Article 20 is completed by the Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) of 22 December 1989 (guidance and coordination act on the construction of residential healthcare facilities for non-self-sufficient older persons) and by Ministry of Health Ministerial Decree (DM) No. 321 of 13 September 1988 (technical standards for healthcare buildings), which are systematically referred to in subsequent regional implementing legislation, for example in Piedmont's rules on social-care and healthcare facilities (Piedmont Regional Council Resolution – DGR – 45-4248/2012) and in the Sicilian standards (Decree of the President of the Sicilian Region – D.P.R.S. – of 25 October 1999).
en_overlay.rsa-nazionale-02:
Minimum requirements: Presidential Decree (DPR) of 14 January 1997

The Presidential Decree (DPR) of 14 January 1997, "Approval of the policy and coordination act addressed to the Regions and to the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano concerning the minimum structural, technological and organisational requirements for the provision of healthcare activities by public and private facilities" constitutes the national framework of minimum requirements for the operating authorisation of healthcare activities, including non-hospital residential care. All regional rules on the authorisation and accreditation of nursing homes (RSA, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali) formally derive from this policy and coordination act, read in conjunction with Articles 8-bis, 8-ter and 8-quater of Legislative Decree (Lgs.D.) 502/1992: see, among others, Veneto Regional Law (RL) 22/2002 and Abruzzo Regional Law 32/2007.
en_overlay.rsa-nazionale-03:
Social and health care services and cost-sharing: Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) of 14 February 2001 and DPCM of 29 November 2001

The Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) of 14 February 2001 ("Guidance and coordination act on social and health care services") introduces the distinction between health services of social relevance, social services of health relevance and highly integrated social and health care services. It allocates costs accordingly between the National Health Service (SSN) and the user or municipality. It is expressly cited, for example, in Sicilian Regional Councillor's Decree (D.A.) No. 209 of 16 March 2022.
The first decree on the Essential Levels of Care (LEA) is the DPCM of 29 November 2001 "Definition of the Essential Levels of Care", published in the Official Gazette on 8 February 2002. (Methodological note: the brief referred to "DPCM of 21 November 2001"; the act actually in force on the LEA is dated 29 November 2001.) It places residential care for non-self-sufficient older persons within district-level care and sets the cost-sharing quotas: 50% health service / 50% user–municipality for long-term maintenance nursing homes, or RSAs; 100% borne by the SSN for intensive treatment.
en_overlay.rsa-nazionale-04:
The Essential Levels of Care (LEA) in force: Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) of 12 January 2017, Article 30

The Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) of 12 January 2017 "Definition and updating of the Essential Levels of Care, referred to in Article 1, paragraph 7, of Legislative Decree no. 502 of 30 December 1992" — whose annexes are published by the Ministry of Health — sets out, in Article 30 ("Residential and semi-residential social and health care for non-self-sufficient persons"), the current national taxonomy of residential treatments, structured into the following levels:
 | | Code | Treatment | National Health Service (SSN) share of costs
 | R1 | Extensive treatments for care and functional maintenance requiring a high level of healthcare input — ALS, vegetative states, assisted ventilation, artificial nutrition | 100%
 | R2 | Extensive treatments for care and functional recovery for non-self-sufficient persons with a high need for healthcare protection | 50%
 | R2D | Extensive treatments for persons with dementia and behavioural disorders | 50%
 | R3 | Long-term care, functional recovery and functional maintenance treatments, including the unit for persons with a lower level of need | 50%
The qualifying standards for R1 units published by the Ministry of Health provide for 24-hour on-call medical cover, a medical presence of approximately 300 minutes/day per unit, 24-hour nursing care, and overall care exceeding 210 minutes/day per resident, of which more than 90 minutes is nursing care (Ministry of Health, residential care standards). This R1/R2/R2D/R3 grid was adopted almost verbatim by the Regions in their post-2017 regulations: see the Apulia Regional Regulation 4/2019, the Campania Decree no. 74 of 9 October 2019, the Marche requirements manual annexed to Regional Council Resolution (DGR) 938/2020 and Basilicata DGR 1218/2017 (the latter text is taken from an unofficial publishing source).
en_overlay.rsa-nazionale-05:
The Long-Term Care Reform: Law 33/2023 and Legislative Decree 29/2024

Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, "Delegation of Powers to the Government on Policies for Older Persons" delegated to the Government the task of reorganising the entire system of care for older persons. It placed particular emphasis on the integration of health and social care, unified multidimensional assessment, home-based care and the upgrading of residential services.
The implementing decree is Legislative Decree No. 29 of 15 March 2024, "Provisions on Policies for Older Persons, Implementing the Delegation Referred to in Articles 3, 4 and 5 of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023". It establishes the National System for the Non-Self-Sufficient Older Population (SNAA), unified multidimensional assessment through the Single Points of Access (PUA) and the experimental Universal Benefit (Prestazione Universale). It also provides for updated requirements and standards for residential and semi-residential services for older persons. This entails progressively moving beyond the purely "institutional" model in favour of facilities organised into small-scale units and light residential solutions such as co-housing, senior housing and sheltered housing.
en_overlay.rsa-nazionale-06:
The National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) context: Ministerial Decree (DM) No. 77 of 23 May 2022

Ministerial Decree No. 77 of 23 May 2022, "Regulation defining models and standards for the development of community-based care within the National Health Service", which implements Mission 6 of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), redefines the community care network (Community Houses, Community Hospitals, Territorial Operations Centres – COT, Integrated Home Care – ADI). It is the main driver of the intense regional regulatory updating carried out in 2022–2025 on non-hospital residential care, with direct effects on the reclassification of nursing homes – RSA, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali (see, for example, Umbria Regional Regulation 2/2022 and Veneto Regional Council Resolution 1720 of 30 December 2022).
en_overlay.rsa-nazionale-07:
Cross-cutting note on legislative competence

Nursing homes (RSA, Residenze Sanitarie Assistenziali) fall within an area of concurrent competence: the State sets the Essential Levels of Care (LEA) and the minimum requirements (Art. 117, para. 2, letter m of the Constitution), while the Regions regulate operating authorisation, accreditation, classification, tariffs and staffing standards. Purely social-care facilities (rest homes, residential group homes, family-type care homes, hotel-style residences) instead remain under exclusively regional competence, with national reference points in Law 328/2000 and in Ministerial Decree (DM) No. 308 of 21 May 2001 (minimum requirements for residential and semi-residential facilities), which is referred to, for example, by Abruzzo Regional Law (RL) 2/2005, Art. 5 and by Piedmont Regional Council Resolution (DGR) 12129/2009. This results in the marked terminological heterogeneity documented in Part II: the same care function takes on different names (RSA, Casa residenza, Centro di servizi, Residenza protetta, Residenza per anziani, Casa protetta) from one Region to another.
